label: Bible Study
prompt: The _____ is far spent, the day is at hand: let us therefore cast off the works of darkness, and let us put on the armour of light.
verse: The night is far spent, the day is at hand: let us therefore cast off the works of darkness, and let us put on the armour of light.
note: Wake-up call — the night's nearly over, so dress for the day in the armour of light.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: Truly the light is _____, and a pleasant thing it is for the eyes to behold the sun:
verse: Truly the light is sweet, and a pleasant thing it is for the eyes to behold the sun:
note: Even the Preacher, who called everything vanity, admits it: light is sweet, and sunshine a pleasant thing.

label: Sunday School
prompt: And being in Bethany in the house of Simon the leper, as he sat at meat, there came a woman having an alabaster box of ointment of _____ very precious; and she brake the box, and poured it on his head.
verse: And being in Bethany in the house of Simon the leper, as he sat at meat, there came a woman having an alabaster box of ointment of spikenard very precious; and she brake the box, and poured it on his head.
note: Spikenard was a very precious ointment — and the woman broke the whole alabaster box and poured it on Jesus' head.

label: Deep Water
prompt: For I am in a strait betwixt two, having a desire to _____, and to be with Christ; which is far better:
verse: For I am in a strait betwixt two, having a desire to depart, and to be with Christ; which is far better:
note: Writing in chains, Paul is torn: heaven is far better, but the Philippians still need him here.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: So the shipmaster came to him, and said unto him, What meanest thou, O _____? arise, call upon thy God, if so be that God will think upon us, that we perish not.
verse: So the shipmaster came to him, and said unto him, What meanest thou, O sleeper? arise, call upon thy God, if so be that God will think upon us, that we perish not.
note: Mid-storm, a pagan shipmaster had to wake the prophet: 'What meanest thou, O sleeper? arise, call upon thy God.'
